question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated control as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, chairman of the Central Military Commission, and president underpins the near-certain trader consensus against removal before 2027. Recent military leadership purges and loyalist appointments have further centralized authority without visible factional challenges or health signals that might prompt elite realignment, while policy continuity on economic planning and public initiatives through mid-2026 aligns with historical patterns of leadership shifts occurring only at scheduled party congresses. The 21st National Congress expected later in 2027 remains the primary venue for any succession signals rather than abrupt ouster. Unforeseen medical events, a severe economic downturn fostering internal consensus against him, or an external crisis eroding elite cohesion before year-end could still alter the outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description: The crowded 2028 Democratic field remains tightly contested on prediction markets, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff clustered at the top amid broad uncertainty over who will enter the race. The DNC's August approval of a revised primary calendar—starting with South Carolina on January 22, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia—has shifted early-state dynamics toward more diverse electorates, while national polls continue to show Kamala Harris ahead in many surveys. Traders appear to weigh factors such as progressive momentum for Ocasio-Cortez in battleground polling, Newsom's term-limited status and national profile, and Ossoff's Senate positioning, alongside questions of electability against the incumbent Republican ticket. Midterm Senate outcomes, candidate announcements after November 2026, and early fundraising will likely begin separating contenders in this still-fluid contest.
